q: Materials which have an electrical resistance that lies between the high resistance values of insulators and the low resistance values of metals are called ______.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. Materials which have an electrical resistance that lies between the high resistance values of insulators and the low resistance values of metals are called semiconductors. Conductors or insulators is not this quantity.

q: In semiconductors, the charge carriers are ______.
e: In a semiconductor both electrons and positive holes carry charge. In semiconductors, the charge carriers are electrons and positive holes. Only electrons or only positive holes is not this quantity.

q: A vacancy which is left by an electron in the semiconductor atom is called a ______.
e: A missing valence electron is a positive hole. The hole behaves like a positive charge. A vacancy which is left by an electron in the semiconductor atom is called a positive hole. Do not trade positive hole for free electron or valence gap.

q: Pure semiconductors have poor conductivity at normal temperature because ______.
a: the number of electrons and holes is relatively few
they are made of non-metallic elements
e: A pure semiconductor has few electrons and holes at room temperature, so it conducts poorly. Pure semiconductors have poor conductivity at normal temperature because the number of electrons and holes is relatively few. They contain no charge carriers or they are made of non-metallic elements is not this quantity.

q: When arsenic atoms are added to pure germanium or silicon, the resulting semiconductor is called ______.
e: A group-V donor such as arsenic makes an n-type semiconductor. Electrons are the majority carriers. When arsenic atoms are added to pure germanium or silicon, the resulting semiconductor is called n-type semiconductor. P-type semiconductor or compound semiconductor is not this quantity.

q: In an n-type semiconductor, the majority charge carriers are ______.
e: In a semiconductor both electrons and positive holes carry charge. In an n-type semiconductor, the majority charge carriers are electrons. Positive holes or protons is not this quantity.

q: When indium atoms are added to pure silicon or germanium, the resulting semiconductor is called ______.
e: Semiconductors use electrons and holes. Doping makes n-type or p-type; a diode rectifies. When indium atoms are added to pure silicon or germanium, the resulting semiconductor is called p-type semiconductor. N-type semiconductor or intrinsic semiconductor is not this quantity.

q: In a p-type semiconductor, the majority charge carriers are ______.
e: In a semiconductor both electrons and positive holes carry charge. In a p-type semiconductor, the majority charge carriers are positive holes. Electrons or neutrons is not this quantity.

q: Germanium and silicon are examples of ______.
e: Germanium and silicon are examples of elemental semiconductors. Compound semiconductors or insulators is not this quantity.

q: Gallium arsenide (GaAs) is an example of a ______.
e: Ge and Si are elemental semiconductors. GaAs and CdTe are compound semiconductors. Gallium arsenide (GaAs) is an example of a compound semiconductor. Metallic conductor or pure insulator is not this quantity.

q: The process of adding impurity atoms to a pure semiconductor to increase its conductivity is called ______.
e: A little donor or acceptor impurity, doping, makes n-type or p-type material and raises conductivity. The process of adding impurity atoms to a pure semiconductor to increase its conductivity is called doping. Do not trade doping for ionization or excitation.

q: A boundary formed between p-type and n-type semiconductors is called a ______.
e: A group-V donor such as arsenic makes an n-type semiconductor. Electrons are the majority carriers. A boundary formed between p-type and n-type semiconductors is called a p-n junction. Depletion layer or bias region is not this quantity.

q: A device which consists of a p-n junction is called a ______.
e: A p-n junction conducts easily one way and blocks the other. That is a diode. A device which consists of a p-n junction is called a p-n junction diode. Transistor or rectifier is not this quantity.

q: When the positive terminal of a battery is connected to the p-type and the negative to the n-type semiconductor, the diode is said to be ______.
e: A group-V donor such as arsenic makes an n-type semiconductor. Electrons are the majority carriers. When the positive terminal of a battery is connected to the p-type and the negative to the n-type semiconductor, the diode is said to be forward-biased. Do not trade forward-biased for reverse-biased or unbiased.

q: When the negative terminal of a battery is connected to the p-type and the positive to the n-type semiconductor, the diode is said to be ______.
e: A group-V donor such as arsenic makes an n-type semiconductor. Electrons are the majority carriers. When the negative terminal of a battery is connected to the p-type and the positive to the n-type semiconductor, the diode is said to be reverse-biased. Forward-biased or neutral is not this quantity.

q: In a forward-biased p-n junction diode, ______.
e: A p-n junction conducts easily one way and blocks the other. That is a diode. In a forward-biased p-n junction diode, a large current flows. No current flows or only minority carriers flow is not this quantity.

q: In a reverse-biased p-n junction diode, ______.
a: only a very small reverse current flows
current flows equally in both directions
e: A p-n junction conducts easily one way and blocks the other. That is a diode. In a reverse-biased p-n junction diode, only a very small reverse current flows. A large current flows or current flows equally in both directions is not this quantity.

q: Anode and cathode of an unconnected p-n junction are not at the same electric potential because ______.
a: there is initially a potential difference across the junction
e: Potential is work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity, V = W/q. Anode and cathode of an unconnected p-n junction are not at the same electric potential because there is initially a potential difference across the junction. Do not trade there is initially a potential difference across the junction for external voltage is applied or the materials are different.

q: A rectifier is a device which converts ______.
e: A rectifier turns AC into one-way current. Two diodes on opposite half-cycles make a full-wave rectifier. A rectifier is a device which converts AC to unidirectional current (DC). Do not trade AC to unidirectional current (DC) for DC to AC or high voltage to low voltage.

q: Diodes can be used as rectifiers because ______.
a: current flows in one direction only
e: A p-n junction conducts easily one way and blocks the other. That is a diode. Diodes can be used as rectifiers because current flows in one direction only. Do not trade current flows in one direction only for they amplify signals or they store electric charge.

q: A half-wave rectifier uses ______ diode(s).
e: A p-n junction conducts easily one way and blocks the other. That is a diode. A half-wave rectifier uses one diode(s). Do not trade one for two or four.

q: A full-wave rectifier uses ______ diode(s).
e: A p-n junction conducts easily one way and blocks the other. That is a diode. A full-wave rectifier uses two diode(s). Do not trade two for one or three.

q: In a half-wave rectifier, current flows through the load resistor during ______.
a: both halves of the AC cycle
only the first half of the AC cycle
e: A rectifier turns AC into one-way current. Two diodes on opposite half-cycles make a full-wave rectifier. In a half-wave rectifier, current flows through the load resistor during only the first half of the AC cycle. Do not trade only the first half of the AC cycle for both halves of the AC cycle or only when voltage is zero.

q: In a full-wave rectifier, current flows through the load resistor during ______.
e: A rectifier turns AC into one-way current. Two diodes on opposite half-cycles make a full-wave rectifier. In a full-wave rectifier, current flows through the load resistor during both half-cycles. Do not trade both half-cycles for only the positive half-cycle or only the negative half-cycle.

q: Rectifiers are used in the power supply units of devices such as ______.
a: radio, television, and mobile phone chargers
e: A rectifier turns AC into one-way current. Two diodes on opposite half-cycles make a full-wave rectifier. Rectifiers are used in the power supply units of devices such as radio, television, and mobile phone chargers. Do not trade radio, television, and mobile phone chargers for electric heaters or incandescent bulbs.

q: A transistor is a semiconductor device which works as a(n) ______.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. A transistor is a semiconductor device which works as a(n) amplifier. Oscillator or insulator is not this quantity.

q: The transistor was invented in ______ by Shockley, Bardeen and Brattain.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. The transistor was invented in 1949 by Shockley, Bardeen and Brattain. Do not trade 1949 for 1947 or 1952.

q: A pnp transistor consists of ______.
a: two n-layers with a p-layer in between
two p-layers with an n-layer in between
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. A pnp transistor consists of two p-layers with an n-layer in between. Two n-layers with a p-layer in between or three p-layers is not this quantity.

q: An npn transistor consists of ______.
a: two p-layers with an n-layer in between
two n-layers with a p-layer in between
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. An npn transistor consists of two n-layers with a p-layer in between. Do not trade two n-layers with a p-layer in between for two p-layers with an n-layer in between or three n-layers.

q: The three electrodes of a transistor are called ______.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. The three electrodes of a transistor are called emitter, base, collector. Do not trade emitter, base, collector for anode, cathode, grid or source, drain, gate.

q: In a transistor biasing circuit, the relationship among currents is ______.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. In a transistor biasing circuit, the relationship among currents is I_E = I_C + I_B. I_C = I_E + I_B or I_B = I_E + I_C is a different relation from I_E = I_C + I_B.

q: In a typical transistor, the base current $I_B$ is approximately ______ of the emitter current $I_E$.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. In a typical transistor, the base current I_B is approximately 0.02 I_E of the emitter current I_E. Do not trade 0.02 I_E for 0.5 I_E or 0.98 I_E.

q: The collector current $I_C$ is approximately ______ of the emitter current $I_E$.
e: The collector current I_C is approximately 0.98 I_E of the emitter current I_E. 0.02 i_e or 0.5 i_e is not this quantity.

q: Because a small base current controls a large collector current, a transistor acts as a ______.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. Because a small base current controls a large collector current, a transistor acts as a current amplifier. Do not trade current amplifier for voltage stabilizer or frequency modulator.

q: The emitter junction in a transistor biasing circuit is ______.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. The emitter junction in a transistor biasing circuit is forward-biased. Do not trade forward-biased for reverse-biased or unbiased.

q: The collector junction in a transistor biasing circuit is ______.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. The collector junction in a transistor biasing circuit is reverse-biased. Do not trade reverse-biased for forward-biased or neutral.

q: The resistance of the forward-biased emitter junction is ______.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. The resistance of the forward-biased emitter junction is small. Do not trade small for large or infinite.

q: The resistance of the reverse-biased collector junction is ______.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. The resistance of the reverse-biased collector junction is large. Do not trade large for small or zero.

q: Because power = $I^2R$, and $I_C \approx I_E$ but $R_C > R_E$, the transistor acts as a ______.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. Because power = I²R, and I_C ≈ I_E but R_C > R_E, the transistor acts as a power amplifier. Current limiter or signal filter is not this quantity.

q: The base layer of a transistor is very thin, about ______.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. The base layer of a transistor is very thin, about 10^-3 cm. Do not trade 10^-3 cm for 10^-1 cm or 10^-2 cm.

q: An arrangement whereby connections of electronic components such as resistors, capacitors and transistors are made is called a(n) ______.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. An arrangement whereby connections of electronic components such as resistors, capacitors and transistors are made is called a(n) electronic circuit. Integrated circuit or logic network is not this quantity.

q: In an integrated circuit (IC), all components and connections are made on ______.
e: In an integrated circuit (IC), all components and connections are made on one single semiconductor crystal. A printed circuit board or multiple vacuum tubes is not this quantity.

q: Integrated circuits are used in ______.
a: televisions, computers and advanced electronic devices
e: Integrated circuits are used in televisions, computers and advanced electronic devices. Electric stoves or mechanical watches is not this quantity.

q: Analog electronics involves quantities with ______ values.
e: Analog electronics involves quantities with continuous values. Discrete or binary is not this quantity.

q: Digital electronics involves quantities with ______ values.
e: Digital electronics involves quantities with discrete values. Do not trade discrete for continuous or random.

q: In digital systems, the two states are represented by ______.
e: In digital systems, the two states are represented by HIGH (logic 1) and LOW (logic 0). Do not trade HIGH (logic 1) and LOW (logic 0) for positive and negative current or on and off frequency.

q: The decimal number system is also called the ______ number system.
e: The decimal number system is also called the base 10 number system. Base 2 or binary is not this quantity.

q: The binary number system has a base of ______.
e: The binary number system has a base of 2. 10 or 16 is not this quantity.

q: In the decimal number 28, the value is calculated as ______.
e: In the decimal number 28, the value is calculated as (2 × 10^1) + (8 × 10^0). (2 × 10^0) + (8 × 10^1) or (2 + 8) × 10 is a different relation from (2 × 10^1) + (8 × 10^0).

q: The binary number 1001$_2$ equals ______ in decimal.
e: The binary number 1001_2 equals 9 in decimal. Do not trade 9 for 7 or 8.

q: The decimal number 12 equals ______ in binary.
e: The decimal number 12 equals 1100_2 in binary. 1010_2 or 1110_2 is not this quantity.

q: In a binary whole number, the right-most bit is called the ______.
e: Semiconductors use electrons and holes. Doping makes n-type or p-type; a diode rectifies. In a binary whole number, the right-most bit is called the LSB. Msb or sign bit is not this quantity.

q: In a binary whole number, the left-most bit is called the ______.
e: Semiconductors use electrons and holes. Doping makes n-type or p-type; a diode rectifies. In a binary whole number, the left-most bit is called the MSB. Parity bit or lsb is not this quantity.

q: The smallest unit of memory or instruction in a computer is a ______.
e: The smallest unit of memory or instruction in a computer is a bit. Do not trade bit for byte or word.

q: A group of 8 bits is called a ______.
e: A group of 8 bits is called a byte. Do not trade byte for kilobyte or nibble.

q: One kilobyte equals ______ bytes.
e: One kilobyte equals 1024 bytes. 1000 or 2048 is not this quantity.

q: One megabyte equals ______ kilobytes.
e: One megabyte equals 1024 kilobytes. Do not trade 1024 for 1000 or 512.

q: One gigabyte equals ______ megabytes.
e: One gigabyte equals 1024 megabytes. 1000 or 2048 is not this quantity.

q: One terabyte equals ______ gigabytes.
e: One terabyte equals 1024 gigabytes. 1000 or 512 is not this quantity.

q: The letter 'A' requires ______ of storage.
e: The letter 'A' requires 1 byte of storage. 1 bit or 1 nibble is not this quantity.

q: A logic gate is an electronic device which takes information from the environment, makes a decision, and then gives out the ______.
e: A logic gate is an electronic device which takes information from the environment, makes a decision, and then gives out the result. Input or voltage is not this quantity.

q: Logic gates are commonly built using ______.
e: Logic gates are commonly built using small integrated circuits (ICs). Do not trade small integrated circuits (ICs) for vacuum tubes or mechanical relays.

q: The five common logic gates are ______.
e: The five common logic gates are AND, OR, NAND, NOR, NOT. Do not trade AND, OR, NAND, NOR, NOT for AND, OR, XOR, XNOR, BUFFER or ADD, SUB, MUL, DIV, MOD.

q: A NOT gate has ______ input(s).
e: A NOT gate has one input(s). Two or three is not this quantity.

q: For a 2-input AND gate, the output is HIGH only when ______.
e: For a 2-input AND gate, the output is HIGH only when both inputs are HIGH. Do not trade both inputs are HIGH for both inputs are LOW or either input is HIGH.

q: For a 2-input OR gate, the output is LOW only when ______.
e: For a 2-input OR gate, the output is LOW only when both inputs are LOW. Both inputs are high or either input is high is not this quantity.

q: For a 2-input NAND gate, the output is LOW only when ______.
e: For a 2-input NAND gate, the output is LOW only when both inputs are HIGH. Do not trade both inputs are HIGH for both inputs are LOW or either input is LOW.

q: For a 2-input NOR gate, the output is HIGH only when ______.
e: For a 2-input NOR gate, the output is HIGH only when both inputs are LOW. Both inputs are high or either input is high is not this quantity.

q: The Boolean expression for a 2-input AND gate is ______.
e: The Boolean expression for a 2-input AND gate is X = AB. X = A + B or X = AB is a different relation from X = AB.

q: The Boolean expression for a 2-input OR gate is ______.
e: The Boolean expression for a 2-input OR gate is X = A + B. X = AB or X = A + B is a different relation from X = A + B. X = a + b is what this sentence is naming. Stay with the quantity named in this sentence.

q: The Boolean expression for a 2-input NAND gate is ______.
e: The Boolean expression for a 2-input NAND gate is X = AB. X = AB or X = A + B is a different relation from X = AB.

q: The Boolean expression for a 2-input NOR gate is ______.
e: The Boolean expression for a 2-input NOR gate is X = A + B. X = AB or X = A + B is a different relation from X = A + B. X = a + b is what this sentence is naming. Stay with the quantity named in this sentence.

q: The Boolean expression for a NOT gate is ______.
e: The Boolean expression for a NOT gate is X = A. X = A or X = A + 1 is a different relation from X = A. X = a is what this sentence is naming. Stay with the quantity named in this sentence.

q: NAND and NOR gates are called universal gates because they ______.
a: can replace any other gate type when combined
e: NAND and NOR gates are called universal gates because they can replace any other gate type when combined. Consume less power or are faster than others is not this quantity.

q: The inverter (NOT gate) changes a LOW input to a ______ output.
e: The inverter (NOT gate) changes a LOW input to a HIGH output. Low or zero is not this quantity.

q: A basic 2-input logic circuit has a HIGH on one input and a LOW on the other, and the output is HIGH. The gate is most likely a(n) ______.
e: A basic 2-input logic circuit has a HIGH on one input and a LOW on the other, and the output is HIGH. The gate is most likely a(n) OR gate. And gate or nand gate is not this quantity.

q: A logic circuit requires HIGHs on all its inputs to make the output HIGH. This describes a(n) ______.
e: A logic circuit requires HIGHs on all its inputs to make the output HIGH. This describes a(n) AND gate. Do not trade AND gate for OR gate or NOR gate.

q: An OR gate can be constructed using ______ NAND gates.
e: An OR gate can be constructed using three NAND gates. Do not trade three for two or four.

q: A NOT gate can be constructed using ______ NAND gate(s).
e: A NOT gate can be constructed using one NAND gate(s). Two or three is not this quantity.

q: An AND gate can be constructed using ______ NAND gates.
e: An AND gate can be constructed using two NAND gates. Do not trade two for one or three.

q: A NOR gate can be constructed using ______ NAND gates.
e: A NOR gate can be constructed using four NAND gates. Three or five is not this quantity.
